newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel worsens on dismal demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel worsens on dismal demand.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel prices slipped again on Wednesday as refiners' continued preference for running cheap crude cut the bottom out of demand, traders said.
A 30,000 tonne cargo of good quality low sulphur straight-run was heard to have traded out of Britain into southern France on Tuesday for $94 fob.
That deal undercut other offer levels pegged at around $95 and confirmed the product's general weakness. U.S. interest was reported at around $92, but no business was seen at that level.
Availability is good, with at least 80,000 tonnes on offer for mid-month.
With the economics of running crude through refineries so strong, demand for Russian straight-run has also collapsed.
"We're in a real spiral downward for resid at the moment," said one trader. "There's no interest, that's the short and sweet of it."
An E-4 out of Klaipeda already afloat, with 1.5 percent water content, was heard being offered at 3 means flat with a quality discount.
An M40 was loading out of St.Petersburg and having trouble securing a buyer. The E-4 and M-40 were both seen eventually heading for the blending and bunker market.
The Hope A out of Ventspils, and a further M-100, were also on offer, the latter at an optimistic 2 means +$5, one trader said.
A further five to six cargoes are seen available in the second half of April.
